# Superior (01, writer) — BAD-007

## Brief
Fix two gaps in docs/RELEASING.md (BadTakes), in the worktree the session is in (branch fix/bad-007-releasing-gaps). Docs-only change; no scripts/worktree-init.sh needed unless the implementing-changes skill says a docs change needs more.

1. Section 5 (Collect the Windows artifacts, ~line 372). `gh run download … --dir /tmp/bt-win` never clears the directory, and section 6 then runs `cp /tmp/bt-win/*/* dist/release/`, so a previous release's Windows files still in /tmp/bt-win get staged beside the new ones. Observed on 2026-09-14 during 0.13.4: /tmp/bt-win still held Bad-Takes-0.13.3-x64-setup.exe, the 0.13.3 win zip and latest.yml. Add `rm -rf /tmp/bt-win` before the download, with one short sentence of why in the doc's own voice. Check section 6's `mkdir -p dist/release` for the same defect (stale files from an earlier release would be uploaded by section 7's `ls dist/release/*`); if nothing clears it, clear it the same way.

2. Section 7 (Publish, ~line 437). `gh release create` passes a generic `--notes "Bad Takes v<X.Y.Z> — …"` and no `--title`. That contradicts the cutting-a-release skill (.claude/skills/cutting-a-release/SKILL.md, "The internal record" and "The public changelog": the body is published from docs/release-notes/<version>/body.md) and Eric's rule that a release title is the bare version (`v0.13.0`, never `Bad Takes v0.13.0`). Replace with `--title "v<X.Y.Z>" --notes-file docs/release-notes/<X.Y.Z>/body.md`. The skill also says order matters: the artwork is pushed to BadTakes-releases (scripts/sync-releases-repo.js) before a body that references it is published, or the release renders broken images. Make sure section 7 says that prerequisite, pointing at the skill rather than duplicating it; if RELEASING.md already has a step for it, just reference that.

Keep the edit minimal and in the file's existing style (prose paragraphs, fenced bash). Do not restructure other sections. Anything else wrong you notice outside these two sections: file a proposal, don't fix it.

Verify: reread both sections as a release-cutter would; confirm the commands are copy-pasteable and the section numbering and cross-references (e.g. "step 7" mentioned elsewhere, ~line 69) still hold. `git diff` should touch only docs/RELEASING.md.
